# Decision history — save-your-skin

Every revision of every `decision` record, plus every terminal revision of any other
normative record. Grouped by key, revisions newest first, keys in key order.

This is the only generated view that includes archived records (D-018). It is the
project's memory of what it used to think, and it is why superseded and withdrawn records
are kept rather than deleted.

**3 decision keys, 4 decision revisions · 1 terminal normative record from elsewhere**

## Decisions

### lege.decision.renderer-boundary

#### Revision 2 — The viewer consumes a frame snapshot

`active` · `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/2` · scope `path "lege/**"` · topic `renderer-boundary`

The viewer reads an immutable frame snapshot produced by the simulator at each
tick boundary. It does not call into the simulator, and no engine type appears
in a viewer signature.

**Context** — Revision 1 put engine types in viewer signatures and made the viewer
untestable in isolation. The text-layout question turned on the same boundary,
so both were settled together.

**Consequences** — One extra allocation and copy per frame, measured at 0.4 ms against
the 16 ms budget. Accepted. The snapshot type is now a third thing to keep in step when
simulator state changes, which the tandem-work policy already covers.

- `#no-engine-types` — No engine type appears in any public viewer signature.
  Supported by `@lege.evidence.boundary-lint-pass/1`.

**Retired claims** — `direct-calls`, which revision 1 defined. A reference to
`@lege.decision.renderer-boundary#direct-calls` therefore reports "anchor retired at
revision 2" rather than "not found" (D-011).

**supersedes** `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/1` ·
**resolves** `@lege.question.text-rendering-owner/1` ·
**implements** `@lege.req.no-engine-types-in-viewer/1` ·
**derived_from** `@lege.obs.viewer-imports-engine/1`

The `derived_from` edge points at a `disproven` observation, and that is deliberate. The
decision really was derived from the finding that the viewer imported engine types; that
finding has since been disproven by the boundary lint, which is the point. Recording the
provenance is more honest than hiding it, and V-019 does not restrict `derived_from` to
live targets.

#### Revision 1 — The viewer calls the simulator directly

`superseded` · `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/1` · scope `path "lege/**"` · topic `renderer-boundary`

The viewer calls simulator entry points directly at each tick boundary and
reads state through them.

**Context** — Chosen for the walking skeleton, when there was no frame snapshot to read
and no second consumer of simulator state.

- `#direct-calls` — The viewer calls simulator entry points directly; there is no
  intermediate representation of frame state. *(retired at revision 2)*

Superseded by `@lege.decision.renderer-boundary/2`.

### sim.decision.timestep-4ms

#### Revision 1 — Fix the simulator timestep at 4 ms

`proposed` · `@sim.decision.timestep-4ms/1` · scope `path "sim/src/step.rs"` · topic `timestep-length`

The simulator steps at 4 ms, giving four steps per rendered frame at 60 Hz.

**Context** — The current 8 ms step is visible as input latency in the day loop. 4 ms
halves it and doubles the per-frame simulation cost.

**Consequences** — Four steps per frame instead of two. Whether that fits the frame
budget is exactly what is unresolved, which is why this is still a proposal.

**depends_on** `@sys.constraint.frame-budget-16ms/1` ·
**implements** `@sim.req.fixed-timestep/1`

**Blocked by** `@sim.question.timestep-vs-budget/1`
([OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](OPEN-QUESTIONS.md#does-a-4-ms-timestep-fit-the-frame-budget))

Still `proposed`, and correctly so: the question that decides it has not been answered.
A `proposed` decision is a decision the project has written down and not yet made.

### sys.decision.view-generation

#### Revision 1 — Views are generated and committed

`active` · `@sys.decision.view-generation/1` · scope `path "docs/generated/**"` · topic `view-generation`

`akr build` writes the six generated views into docs/generated, and those files
are committed. CI runs `akr check --views-current` and fails on any difference.

**Context** — The alternative was generating views on demand and gitignoring them, which
would leave anyone reading the repository on the web with nothing.

**Consequences** — Regenerated views conflict on merge. The conflict is always resolved
by rebuilding, never by hand-merging, and that procedure belongs in AGENTS.md.

**implements** `@sys.policy.no-hand-edited-views/1`

This decision is the reason the file you are reading exists, and the reason it carries a
banner.

## Retired normative records

Terminal revisions of normative records that are not decisions. These no longer govern
anything, still resolve, and appear in no other view.

### sys.policy.weekly-demo

#### Revision 1 — Weekly demo build every Friday

`withdrawn` · `@sys.policy.weekly-demo/1` · scope `all` · topic `demo-cadence` · archived

A playable build is cut every Friday and posted for the team to play over the
weekend.

**Rationale** — Intended to keep the day loop honest by making someone play it weekly.

Withdrawn, not deleted. The practice really was in force and really was abandoned;
deleting the record would lose the fact that the project once worked this way and
stopped. It lives in `.akr/archive/sys/policies-archived.akr`, still resolves, and is
excluded from every view but this one.

Its `topic demo-cadence` is now unclaimed, so a future policy may take it without
tripping V-013 — exclusivity is between *live* records only.
